subject.title: [Bug] Gateway restart races its own startup-migration lease; systemd start-limit exhausts ~10x before the lease expires → indefinite outage

question: Should OpenClaw resolve a live startup-migration lease collision by waiting/retrying in the gateway process, by changing supervisor retry semantics, or by combining a lifecycle release with bounded retry?
rationale: Each option changes startup latency, shutdown guarantees, and the separation between transient migration contention and permanent gateway failures; the report establishes the failure but not the intended product recovery contract.

options.title: Bounded gateway retry
options.body: Treat the existing lease as a transient condition, wait or retry acquisition up to a defined bound, and retain the existing supervisor handling for genuine permanent failures.

options.title: Supervisor-managed retry
options.body: Return a documented retry-later outcome and revise the generated service policy so its retry window exceeds the maximum legitimate lease duration.

options.title: Shutdown release plus fallback
options.body: Release the lease during graceful shutdown and retain a bounded retry path for crashes or forced termination that cannot run shutdown cleanup.

recommendation.title: Bounded gateway retry
recommendation.body: Treat the existing lease as a transient condition, wait or retry acquisition up to a defined bound, and retain the existing supervisor handling for genuine permanent failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has the most concrete incident timing and deployment evidence available in this review, though ownership should be reassigned after source-history inspection.
